dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: They were successfully recovered after the fact. It sure took a lot of effort to transport them.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: After the inspection, we found both prototypes needed to be scrapped. They hadn't been maintained for a long time, plus...

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Oh, I didn't mean to blame you. Mr. Maillardet has some new toys now and has completely forgotten about the prototypes.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: He even delegated the recovery and inspection work. I had hoped I would have a chance to meet him, but it looks like I'll need to find an opportunity to visit Erinnyes for that...

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Oh, that... I was quite surprised that Mr. Bossuet didn't take it back to Petrichor.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: After all, if it gets left here, who knows when someone will spill ink or some even harder to clean fluid on it...

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: I do have a few suspects in mind, but I expect that in the end Chisseray will be chosen to go to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Goodness me, what am I doing! It's best not to say what you're really thinking in this kind of workplace.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Then I hope you have a most wonderful day.

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Objectively speaking, the Icewind Suite is of less commercial value than Fonta. After all, the original proposal came from Mr. Bossuet...

dialogues.speaker: Sevigne
dialogues.text: Mr. Maillardet took it over and then added his own color... But if you ask me, the undertaking is much like the man himself. How to put it kindly? There's room for development?
